newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Attorney for Mass. collects record $75 mln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Attorney for Mass. collects record $75 mln.

text.p: The U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts on Monday said a record $75.1 million was recovered in 1996, in part because Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and Lazard Freres & Co settled a controversial municipal bond case.

The $24 million civil settlement by Merrill and Lazard helped push the amount collected by the U.S. Attorney's office in the 1996 federal fiscal year sharply higher than the $58.6 million record set the previous year.

"This is a remarkable payback for the taxpayer," said Donald Stern, in prepared remarks. "We have recovered almost five dollars for every dollar invested in the U.S. Attorney's office," he added, noting the annual budget for this U.S. Attorney office is $16 million.

Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres settled the case brought against them over failing to ensure that Mark Ferber, a financial advisor formerly with Lazard, had adequately disclosed he also maintained a separate contract with Merrill to help that firm gain municipal swaps work. Neither firm admitted or denied guilt.
Ferber, who in August was found guilty of 58 counts of federal fraud and corruption charges, is scheduled for sentencing in November, Stern said.
Civil settlements and judgments collected by the U.S. Attorney's office in Massachusetts totaled $46.1 million, while criminal fines, assessments and restitution contributed $26 million.
The significant recoveries included a $15 million fine paid by C.R. Bard, which pled guilty to defrauding federally funded hospitals and Medicare.
